headline: Southeast Asia Declares Victory Over Trachoma, World's Leading Infectious Cause of Blindn…
meta_description: WHO certifies Timor-Leste trachoma-free, making all of Southeast Asia a trachoma-free region of 2 billion people with access to detection and treatment.
summary_short: Timor-Leste's certification as trachoma-free means the entire Southeast Asian region has eliminated the world's leading infectious cause of blindness.
body:
Timor-Leste has become the final piece in Southeast Asia's victory against trachoma, a bacterial infection that has blinded millions throughout history. The World Health Organization recently certified the island nation as having eliminated trachoma as a public health problem, marking a milestone that extends the disease-free status across the entire Southeast Asian region—home to over 2 billion people who now live with minimal risk of contracting the bacteria and with access to medical services capable of detecting and treating it. Caused by Chlamydia trachomatis, repeated infections scar the inner eyelid, turning eyelashes inward and ultimately causing blindness. The disease has long been linked to poverty and inequities in access to water, sanitation, hygiene products, and healthcare.

Timor-Leste's achievement capped a rigorous validation process spanning years. Between 2015 and 2017, investigators examined children on Atauro Island, screened patients at eye clinics nationwide, and conducted house-to-house searches—finding no trace of the disease. A 2025 survey tested nearly 5,000 samples from children aged 1–5 years across all 13 municipalities, confirming no active transmission. The country joins Laos (eliminated 2017), Nepal (2018), Myanmar (2020), India (2024), and others in this achievement.

Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General, praised Timor-Leste's success as a significant step toward the global target of eliminating trachoma worldwide by 2030. The country's approach—combining strong national leadership, rigorous evidence, and integrated health services—demonstrates how limited resources can produce lasting gains when surveillance and coordination span multiple diseases. This Southeast Asian milestone shows what becomes possible when medical access reaches even the most remote communities.
quick_facts: Timor-Leste certified trachoma-free by WHO in 2025
Over 2 billion people in Southeast Asia now protected
2025 survey tested nearly 5,000 children across 13 municipalities
Trachoma is the world's leading infectious cause of blindness
Nine Southeast Asian countries have now eliminated trachoma
